title: Add CI workflow to run check and test
description:
## Summary

Add a GitHub Actions CI workflow that automatically runs linting and tests on pull requests and pushes to `main`.

## Tasks

- [ ] Add a GitHub Actions workflow file (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`)
- [ ] Configure the workflow to run `just check` (lint)
- [ ] Configure the workflow to run `just test` (molecule tests for all roles)
- [ ] Trigger on pull requests and pushes to `main`

## Notes

- The project uses `uv` for Python dependency management and `just` as the task runner
- `just check` runs `ansible-lint` via `uv run --`
- `just test` runs molecule tests for all roles

title: Add opt-out variable for EPEL/CRB repo configuration in r role
description:
## Summary

The \`configure_redhat.yml\` task unconditionally enables EPEL and CRB repositories on RedHat systems. This can conflict with environments that manage repositories via Red Hat Satellite, custom mirrors, or other repo management tools.

## Proposed Fix

Add a boolean variable (e.g., \`r_configure_repos: true\`) that controls whether the role manages repo configuration. Users who manage repos externally can set \`r_configure_repos: false\` to skip this step:

\`\`\`yaml
- name: Configure RedHat repositories
  ansible.builtin.include_tasks: configure_redhat.yml
  when:
    - ansible_facts['os_family'] == 'RedHat'
    - r_versions | length > 0
    - r_configure_repos | bool
\`\`\`

title: Add checksum verification for downloaded R packages
description:
## Summary

The \`get_url\` tasks in the R role download packages from Posit's CDN without verifying checksums. Posit may publish checksums alongside the packages; if so, we should validate them.

## Proposed Fix

1. Check whether Posit publishes SHA256 checksums for r-builds packages (e.g., at \`cdn.posit.co/r/{os}/pkgs/\`)
2. If available, add a \`checksum\` parameter to each \`ansible.builtin.get_url\` task, or add a separate \`ansible.builtin.stat\`/\`ansible.builtin.shell\` checksum verification step

This improves supply chain security by ensuring downloaded packages haven't been tampered with.

title: Install gfortran dependency within the r role (Debian/Ubuntu)
description:
## Summary

R packages from Posit's CDN depend on \`gfortran\` on Debian/Ubuntu systems. Currently, this dependency is installed in Molecule's \`prepare.yml\` (a test-only step), meaning users who run the role on a fresh system will get a confusing package manager error.

## Proposed Fix

Add a prerequisite task in \`roles/r/tasks/install_debian.yml\` (or a shared prerequisites task in \`main.yml\`) to ensure \`gfortran\` is present before attempting R installation:

\`\`\`yaml
- name: Install R prerequisites
  ansible.builtin.apt:
    name: gfortran
    state: present
    update_cache: true
\`\`\`

Once this is added, the \`prepare.yml\` gfortran step can be removed from Molecule.

title: Add input validation to the r role
description:
## Summary

The \`r\` role silently does nothing when \`r_versions\` is empty (the default). Users who forget to set \`r_versions\` get no feedback.

## Proposed Fix

Add an \`assert\` task at the top of \`roles/r/tasks/main.yml\` that fails with a helpful message when \`r_versions\` is empty:

\`\`\`yaml
- name: Assert r_versions is set
  ansible.builtin.assert:
    that: r_versions | length > 0
    fail_msg: "r_versions must contain at least one R version to install (e.g., r_versions: ['4.4.0'])"
\`\`\`

title: Investigate GPG signing for Posit r-builds packages
description:
## Summary

The R role currently uses \`disable_gpg_check: true\` when installing RPM packages on RedHat and SUSE platforms. Investigation suggests the packages from \`cdn.posit.co/r\` are not GPG-signed, which means this flag is suppressing an expected error rather than bypassing real security.

## Action Items

- Confirm with Posit whether r-builds packages are intentionally unsigned
- If packages can be signed, request that GPG signatures be published to the CDN
- Once signed, update the role to import Posit's GPG key and remove \`disable_gpg_check: true\`

## Current Behavior

Both \`install_redhat.yml\` and \`install_suse.yml\` use \`disable_gpg_check: true\` on the dnf/zypper install tasks.

title: Add RHEL 8 to molecule test matrix
description:
## Summary

RHEL 8 is currently excluded from the molecule test matrix because `ansible-core >= 2.20` requires Python 3.9+ on managed nodes, and the Rocky Linux 8 Docker image ships Python 3.6 as the default.

RHEL 8 Maintenance Support ends **May 31, 2029**, so it remains a supported target.

## Possible approaches

1. Add a prepare step that installs `python39` via dnf and sets `ansible_python_interpreter` before the role runs
2. Use a custom Docker image based on `geerlingguy/docker-rockylinux8-ansible` with Python 3.9 pre-installed
3. Pin `ansible-core` to `>=2.15,<2.20` (supports Python 3.8+ on managed nodes) — likely undesirable

Option 1 is probably the right approach but requires careful ordering since `gather_facts` runs before `prepare.yml`.

## Notes

- The role itself supports RHEL 8 — this is purely a testing infrastructure issue
- Related to the `molecule-plugins` / `ansible-core` 2.20 managed node Python requirement

title: Role: Posit Package Manager
description:
## Summary

Create an Ansible role for installing and configuring Posit Package Manager.

## Requirements

Per the [Posit Package Manager admin guide](https://docs.posit.co/rspm/admin/getting-started/requirements.html):

- Install Posit Package Manager from Posit's package repository
- Manage the Package Manager configuration file
- Manage the Package Manager systemd service
- Support licensing activation

## Platform Support

- **RedHat**: RHEL 8, 9 (and derivatives)
- **Debian**: Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04
- **SUSE**: SLES 15
- **Architectures**: x86_64 and aarch64/arm64

title: Role: Python
description:
## Summary

Create an Ansible role for installing Python using pre-built binaries from Posit's Python builds CDN (`cdn.posit.co/python`).

## Requirements

- Install one or more Python versions side-by-side (to `/opt/python/{version}/`)
- Optionally set a default Python version via symlinks to `/usr/local/bin`
- Idempotent — skip installation if the version is already present

## Platform Support

- **RedHat**: RHEL 8, 9, 10 (and derivatives)
- **Debian**: Ubuntu 22.04, 24.04; Debian 12, 13
- **SUSE**: SLES 15.x
- **Architectures**: x86_64 and aarch64/arm64

## Notes

Python is a common dependency for Posit Connect and Posit Workbench. This role should follow the same pattern established by the R role.

title: Role: R
description:
